summary.intent: Extend Callisto's release tooling so nested (non-root) npm and uv workspaces are handled for membership and lockfiles, following the already-open nested Cargo workspace PR #241, and then address the earlier leftover items.
summary.outcome: Implemented nested npm/uv membership and per-directory lockfile refresh in a stacked worktree branch, with locate/apply tests, a real-npm scenario check, docs and changeset updates. Full CI passed at 92.71% coverage, and the stacked PR was committed, pushed and opened. The earlier leftovers were not started.

repo: Callisto is a Rust workspace; the graph logic lives in crates/callisto-graph, with workspace location in src/locate/ (membership.rs, ignore_walk.rs) and version application in src/apply.rs and src/apply/preflight.rs.
`just ci` runs the full pipeline (lint, tests, coverage) and reports a coverage percentage; the nested Cargo PR #241 landed at 92.66% and the stacked npm/uv branch at 92.71%.
Specs are kept in docs/specs/*.json (versioning.json, workspace.json), and user-facing changes need a .changeset/*.md entry.
Root detection requires a marker (package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml or .moon); a repo whose only manifest is native/Cargo.toml fails with E030.

In a root Cargo workspace, the root's `members` and `exclude` still decide membership, so `exclude = ["native"]` keeps native/ unreleased. This was left intentionally so example and fixture workspaces stay excluded.
Private, versionless nested workspace roots need an exemption from the version requirement; the real-npm scenario exposed this.
uv/Python test fixtures must use PEP 440 versions for the bump to succeed.
Lockfile refresh and staging were restructured to work per directory, so each nested workspace refreshes and stages its own lockfile.
workflow: Stack dependent PRs using a separate worktree (EnterWorktree) branched from the previous PR when they touch the same code.
Mutation-check new tests by confirming they fail without the behavior before trusting them.
Validate against real tooling (real cargo, npm, git) in scratch scripts in addition to unit tests; this surfaced edge cases such as versionless private roots.
Run the long CI pipeline in the background and investigate review findings (Codex's ignored-file/git-add concerns) in parallel.
Probe real git behavior (ignored files, mixed ignored paths in one `git add`) with small shell scripts before changing staging logic.
